category: Predictive Maintenance Toolbox > Ensemble Data, Condition Indicators, Machinery Diagnostics & Remaining Useful Life
description: Predictive Maintenance Toolbox functions (plus closely related Signal Processing Toolbox machinery-diagnostics functions) for managing run-to-failure ensembles, designing condition indicators from vibration and nonlinear signal features, ranking features, and estimating remaining useful life (RUL) with degradation, similarity and survival models.

tools.name: fileEnsembleDatastore
tools.description: Creates a datastore that manages an ensemble of machine data stored as one file per member (e.g. one MAT or CSV file per run), with a custom read function and data/condition/independent variable definitions. It is the standard container for condition-monitoring data in Predictive Maintenance Toolbox.
tools.usage:
fensemble = fileEnsembleDatastore(location, fileExtension)
fensemble = fileEnsembleDatastore(location, fileExtension, Name=Value)

parameters.name: location / fileExtension
parameters.description: Folder (or files) and extension such as ".mat" or ".csv".

parameters.name: ReadFcn / WriteToMemberFcn
parameters.description: Functions that read a member into a table and write new variables back.

tools.notes: Use subset and tall for large ensembles, and open the ensemble in Diagnostic Feature Designer to design features interactively.

tools.name: simulationEnsembleDatastore
tools.description: Manages an ensemble of Simulink simulation results (logged signals and parameters) stored in MAT-files, typically produced by generateSimulationEnsemble for fault-injection studies.
tools.usage:
ensemble = simulationEnsembleDatastore(location)
ensemble = simulationEnsembleDatastore(location, Name=Value)

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Folder containing the simulation result files.

parameters.name: DataVariables / ConditionVariables / SelectedVariables
parameters.description: Variable roles, detected from logged data.

tools.notes: Members are read as tables whose signal variables are timetables.

tools.name: generateSimulationEnsemble
tools.description: Runs a Simulink model for each Simulink.SimulationInput (e.g. different fault parameters) and saves the logged results as ensemble members, optionally in parallel.
tools.usage:
[status, E] = generateSimulationEnsemble(simin, location)
[status, E] = generateSimulationEnsemble(simin, location, Name=Value)

parameters.name: UseParallel
parameters.description: Run simulations with Parallel Computing Toolbox.

tools.notes: Requires Simulink. Open results with simulationEnsembleDatastore.

tools.name: workspaceEnsemble
tools.description: Manages ensemble data held in a MATLAB workspace table (one row per member) with data and condition variable roles, as used by code generated from Diagnostic Feature Designer.
tools.usage:
wensemble = workspaceEnsemble(data)
wensemble = workspaceEnsemble(data, Name=Value)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Table whose rows are members and variables hold signals (timetables) and conditions.

tools.example:
ens = workspaceEnsemble(memberTable, DataVariables="Vibration", ConditionVariables="Health");
m = read(ens);
tools.notes: Suited to datasets that fit in memory; use fileEnsembleDatastore for large collections.

tools.name: writeToLastMemberRead
tools.description: Writes new variables (e.g. computed condition indicators) back to the ensemble member most recently read, so features are stored alongside the raw data.
tools.usage:
writeToLastMemberRead(ensemble, data)
writeToLastMemberRead(ensemble, Name, Value)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Table (one row) of variables to write.

tools.notes: For fileEnsembleDatastore, WriteToMemberFcn must be defined. Add the new names to DataVariables to read them later.

tools.name: diagnosticFeatureDesigner
tools.description: Opens the Diagnostic Feature Designer app for importing ensembles, preprocessing signals, extracting time/frequency/rotating-machinery features, ranking them for fault classification or prognostics, and generating MATLAB code for the pipeline.
tools.usage: diagnosticFeatureDesigner
tools.example:
load("pumpEnsembleData.mat")   % table ensemble in the workspace
diagnosticFeatureDesigner
tools.notes: Export ranked features to Classification Learner or generate a function that recomputes features on new data. Health Indicator Designer complements it for prognostics.

tools.name: tsa
tools.description: Computes the time-synchronous average of a vibration signal using tachometer pulses, averaging over shaft rotations to suppress components that are not synchronous with the shaft (gear diagnostics foundation).
tools.usage:
ta = tsa(x, fs, tPulse)
[ta, t, rpm] = tsa(x, fs, tPulse, Name=Value)

parameters.name: NumRotations / Method
parameters.description: Rotations per segment and interpolation/averaging method.

tools.example:
ta = tsa(vib, fs, tachoTimes, NumRotations=1);
d = tsadifference(ta, fs, rpm, [1 2 23]);
tools.notes: Part of Signal Processing Toolbox; the TSA signal feeds tsaregular, tsaresidual and tsadifference for gear condition metrics.

tools.name: tsadifference
tools.description: Computes the difference signal of a time-synchronous averaged signal by removing the shaft orders, gear-mesh orders and their first-order sidebands, leaving components indicative of localized gear tooth faults.
tools.usage:
Y = tsadifference(X, fs, rpm, orderList)
Y = tsadifference(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: orderList
parameters.description: Shaft and gear-mesh orders to filter (e.g. [1 2 NTeeth]).

tools.example:
D = tsadifference(ta, fs, 1800, [1 2 23 46]);
FM4 = kurtosis(D);
tools.notes: tsaregular extracts only the regular (mesh) components, tsaresidual removes mesh orders but keeps sidebands. Metrics such as FM4, NA4 and M6A are computed from these signals.

tools.name: tsaregular
tools.description: Extracts the regular signal of a time-synchronous averaged signal, i.e. the shaft and gear-mesh frequency components and their harmonics, representing healthy periodic gear behavior.
tools.usage:
Y = tsaregular(X, fs, rpm, orderList)
Y = tsaregular(___, Name=Value)
tools.example:
R = tsaregular(ta, fs, 1800, [23 46 69]);
plot(R)
tools.notes: Use with tsaresidual/tsadifference to separate periodic mesh content from fault content.

tools.name: tsaresidual
tools.description: Computes the residual signal of a time-synchronous averaged signal by removing the shaft and gear-mesh components (but not sidebands), highlighting modulation caused by faults.
tools.usage:
Y = tsaresidual(X, fs, rpm, orderList)
Y = tsaresidual(___, Name=Value)
tools.example:
Rs = tsaresidual(ta, fs, 1800, [1 23 46]);
NA4 = kurtosis(Rs);
tools.notes: Residual-based metrics trend as damage progresses.

tools.name: bearingFaultBands
tools.description: Generates frequency bands around the characteristic defect frequencies of a rolling-element bearing (ballpass outer/inner race, ball spin, cage) given its geometry and shaft speed, for spectral fault-band features.
tools.usage:
[FB, info] = bearingFaultBands(FR, NB, DB, DP, beta)
[FB, info] = bearingFaultBands(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: NB / DB / DP / beta
parameters.description: Number of balls, ball diameter, pitch diameter and contact angle (deg).

tools.notes: gearMeshFaultBands does the same for meshing gears; faultBands builds bands from arbitrary frequencies.

tools.name: faultBands
tools.description: Generates frequency bands around user-specified fundamental frequencies, their harmonics and sidebands, for extracting spectral features at known fault frequencies of any machine.
tools.usage:
FB = faultBands(F0, N0)
FB = faultBands(F0, N0, F1, N1)
[FB, info] = faultBands(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: F1 / N1
parameters.description: Sideband spacing frequencies and sideband numbers.

parameters.name: Width / Folding
parameters.description: Band width and folding of negative bands.

tools.notes: Output is an N-by-2 matrix of [low high] band edges.

tools.name: faultBandMetrics
tools.description: Computes spectral metrics (peak amplitude, peak frequency, band power, total band power) of a power spectral density within specified fault frequency bands, producing compact condition indicators.
tools.usage:
spectralMetrics = faultBandMetrics(x, f, FB)
[spectralMetrics, T] = faultBandMetrics(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: x, f
parameters.description: PSD values and frequencies (or a timetable/spectrum).

parameters.name: FB
parameters.description: Bands from faultBands, bearingFaultBands or gearMeshFaultBands.

tools.notes: Compute on envelope spectra (envspectrum) for bearing faults.

tools.name: envspectrum
tools.description: Computes the envelope spectrum of a vibration signal (via Hilbert transform or complex demodulation within a band), revealing bearing defect frequencies that modulate high-frequency resonances.
tools.usage:
[es, f] = envspectrum(x, fs)
[es, f, env, t] = envspectrum(x, fs, Name=Value)
envspectrum(___)

parameters.name: Band
parameters.description: [fLow fHigh] band to envelope, e.g. chosen from a kurtogram.

tools.example:
[es, f] = envspectrum(vib, fs, Band=[2000 5000]);
plot(f, es); xlim([0 500])
tools.notes: Signal Processing Toolbox function. Choose the band with kurtogram or spectralKurtosis.

tools.name: kurtogram
tools.description: Computes and displays the fast kurtogram, i.e. spectral kurtosis over frequency and resolution levels, to find the frequency band where impulsive fault signatures are strongest.
tools.usage:
kurtogram(x, fs)
kurtogram(x, fs, level)
[kgram, f, w, fc, wc, bw] = kurtogram(___)

parameters.name: fc / bw (outputs)
parameters.description: Center frequency and bandwidth of the band with maximum kurtosis.

tools.example:
[~, ~, ~, fc, ~, bw] = kurtogram(vib, fs, 6);
es = envspectrum(vib, fs, Band=[fc-bw/2 fc+bw/2]);
tools.notes: Signal Processing Toolbox function; spectralKurtosis gives the kurtosis at a single resolution.

tools.name: spectralKurtosis
tools.description: Computes spectral kurtosis of a signal or spectrogram, highlighting frequency bands with transient, non-Gaussian content such as bearing impacts, together with a confidence threshold.
tools.usage:
sk = spectralKurtosis(x, fs)
[sk, f, thresh] = spectralKurtosis(___, Name=Value)
spectralKurtosis(___)

parameters.name: ConfidenceLevel
parameters.description: Confidence level for the stationary-Gaussian threshold (default 0.95).

tools.example:
[sk, f, th] = spectralKurtosis(vib, fs, Window=256);
plot(f, sk); yline(th)
tools.notes: Signal Processing Toolbox function (replaces pkurtosis).

tools.name: orderspectrum
tools.description: Computes the average spectrum versus shaft order of a vibration signal measured under varying speed, using an RPM profile to resample into the order domain. Order analysis keeps shaft-related peaks aligned during run-up/down.
tools.usage:
[spec, order] = orderspectrum(x, fs, rpm)
[spec, order] = orderspectrum(___, Name=Value)
orderspectrum(___)

parameters.name: rpm
parameters.description: Rotational speed profile, same length as x.

tools.notes: Signal Processing Toolbox function; ordertrack and rpmtrack estimate order magnitudes and RPM.

tools.name: approximateEntropy
tools.description: Measures the regularity (unpredictability) of a nonlinear time series; lower values indicate more regular signals. Used as a condition indicator for machines whose vibration becomes more irregular with faults.
tools.usage:
approxEnt = approximateEntropy(X)
approxEnt = approximateEntropy(X, lag, dim)
approxEnt = approximateEntropy(___, Radius=r)

parameters.name: lag / dim
parameters.description: Time delay and embedding dimension (estimated automatically if omitted).

tools.example:
x = sin(2*pi*(0:0.01:10)) + 0.1*randn(1,1001);
approximateEntropy(x)
tools.notes: Related nonlinear features: correlationDimension, lyapunovExponent, phaseSpaceReconstruction.

tools.name: correlationDimension
tools.description: Estimates the correlation dimension of a time series, a measure of chaotic signal complexity (dimensionality of the attractor) useful for tracking changes in system dynamics.
tools.usage:
corDim = correlationDimension(X)
corDim = correlationDimension(X, lag, dim)
[corDim, r, C] = correlationDimension(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: MinRadius / MaxRadius / NumPoints
parameters.description: Radius range and number of points for the correlation integral.

tools.example: cd = correlationDimension(vib(1:4000), 10, 3)
tools.notes: Plot C versus r (log-log) to verify the linear scaling region.

tools.name: lyapunovExponent
tools.description: Estimates the largest Lyapunov exponent of a uniformly sampled time series, characterizing the rate at which nearby trajectories diverge; positive values indicate chaos.
tools.usage:
lyapExp = lyapunovExponent(X, fs)
lyapExp = lyapunovExponent(X, fs, lag, dim)
[lyapExp, estLag, estDim] = lyapunovExponent(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: ExpansionRange / MinSeparation
parameters.description: Range of expansion steps for the linear fit and minimum temporal separation.

tools.example: le = lyapunovExponent(x, 100, ExpansionRange=[1 30])
tools.notes: Requires reasonably long, stationary records.

tools.name: phaseSpaceReconstruction
tools.description: Reconstructs the phase space (delay-coordinate embedding) of a time series, estimating the embedding lag and dimension. The reconstructed states feed nonlinear features and visualization of dynamics.
tools.usage:
[XR, eLag, eDim] = phaseSpaceReconstruction(X)
XR = phaseSpaceReconstruction(X, lag, dim)
phaseSpaceReconstruction(___)

parameters.name: lag / dim
parameters.description: Delay and embedding dimension (estimated with mutual information and false nearest neighbors if omitted).

tools.example:
[XR, lag, dim] = phaseSpaceReconstruction(x);
plot3(XR(:,1), XR(:,2), XR(:,3))
tools.notes: Reuse eLag and eDim in approximateEntropy, correlationDimension and lyapunovExponent.

tools.name: tfmoment
tools.description: Computes the joint time-frequency moment of a signal's time-frequency distribution, a compact feature capturing nonstationary behavior. tfsmoment and tftmoment give conditional spectral and temporal moments.
tools.usage:
moment = tfmoment(x, fs, order)
moment = tfmoment(xt, order)
moment = tfmoment(p, fp, tp, order)

parameters.name: p, fp, tp
parameters.description: Precomputed time-frequency distribution, frequencies and times.

tools.example:
m = tfmoment(vib, fs, [1 2]);
sm = tfsmoment(vib, fs, 2);     % instantaneous spectral variance
tools.notes: Useful for machines under transient operating conditions.

tools.name: bhattacharyyaDistance
tools.description: Computes the one-dimensional Bhattacharyya distance between two groups of feature values (e.g. healthy vs. faulty), assuming normal distributions. Used to rank condition indicators by class separability.
tools.usage: d = bhattacharyyaDistance(x1, x2)

parameters.name: x1, x2
parameters.description: Feature values of the two groups.

tools.example: d = bhattacharyyaDistance(featHealthy, featFaulty)
tools.notes: relativeEntropy (KL divergence) is an alternative ranking measure; Diagnostic Feature Designer offers both.

tools.name: monotonicity
tools.description: Quantifies how monotonic the trend of a condition indicator is over the lifetime of multiple run-to-failure members, from 0 (no trend) to 1 (perfectly monotonic). A key criterion for selecting prognostic health indicators.
tools.usage:
Y = monotonicity(X)
Y = monotonicity(X, lifetimeVar, dataVar)
Y = monotonicity(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Cell array of feature histories, table/timetable, or ensemble.

tools.example: Y = monotonicity(featureHistories, WindowSize=5)
tools.notes: Combine with prognosability and trendability; features scoring high on all three make good RUL inputs.

tools.name: prognosability
tools.description: Measures the variability of condition indicator values at failure across members relative to their range; values near 1 mean all members fail at a similar indicator value, making a failure threshold meaningful.
tools.usage:
Y = prognosability(X)
Y = prognosability(X, lifetimeVar, dataVar)
tools.example: p = prognosability(featureHistories)
tools.notes: trendability measures similarity of trajectories across members.

tools.name: trendability
tools.description: Measures the similarity between the trajectories of a condition indicator across run-to-failure members (minimum absolute correlation); high trendability means members degrade along similar paths.
tools.usage:
Y = trendability(X)
Y = trendability(X, lifetimeVar, dataVar)
tools.example: t = trendability(featureHistories)
tools.notes: Members of different lengths are resampled for comparison.

tools.name: exponentialDegradationModel
tools.description: Creates an exponential degradation RUL model h(t) = phi + theta*exp(beta*t + eps) with Bayesian prior on parameters. It is fit to historical run-to-failure data, updated online with new measurements and predicts time to reach a failure threshold with confidence bounds.
tools.usage:
mdl = exponentialDegradationModel
mdl = exponentialDegradationModel(Name=Value)
fit(mdl, data)
update(mdl, data)
[estRUL, ciRUL, pdfRUL] = predictRUL(mdl, threshold)

parameters.name: Theta / Beta / Phi / Rho
parameters.description: Prior parameters (set via fit from historical data).

tools.notes: linearDegradationModel is the linear variant. Use plot(mdl) to view the degradation fit. Deploy with saveRULModelForCoder.

tools.name: linearDegradationModel
tools.description: Creates a linear degradation RUL model h(t) = phi + theta*t + eps with Bayesian parameter updates, for condition indicators that degrade roughly linearly over time.
tools.usage:
mdl = linearDegradationModel
mdl = linearDegradationModel(Name=Value)
fit(mdl, data)
update(mdl, data)
[estRUL, ciRUL, pdfRUL] = predictRUL(mdl, threshold)
tools.notes: restart(mdl) resets the posterior to the prior for a new component.

tools.name: residualSimilarityModel
tools.description: Creates a residual-based similarity RUL model that fits a dynamic (ARX-type) model to each historical run-to-failure member and estimates RUL of a test component from the lifetimes of the most similar members.
tools.usage:
mdl = residualSimilarityModel
mdl = residualSimilarityModel(Name=Value)
fit(mdl, data, lifeTimeVariable, dataVariables)
[estRUL, ciRUL, pdfRUL] = predictRUL(mdl, data)

parameters.name: NumNearestNeighbors
parameters.description: Number of most similar members used (default 10).

parameters.name: Method / Distance
parameters.description: Model structure and residual distance measure.

tools.notes: hashSimilarityModel (feature hashing) and pairwiseSimilarityModel (direct trajectory comparison) are alternative similarity models.

tools.name: hashSimilarityModel
tools.description: Creates a hashed-feature similarity RUL model that summarizes each member's degradation history with hash features (e.g. min, max, mean, power) and predicts RUL from the nearest historical members; scalable to large fleets.
tools.usage:
mdl = hashSimilarityModel
mdl = hashSimilarityModel(Name=Value)
fit(mdl, data, lifeTimeVariable, dataVariables)
estRUL = predictRUL(mdl, data)

parameters.name: HashFunction
parameters.description: Function returning hash features from a member's data.

tools.notes: Faster than pairwise comparison for many members.

tools.name: pairwiseSimilarityModel
tools.description: Creates a pairwise-comparison similarity RUL model that compares the test component's degradation trajectory directly with each historical trajectory (optionally with dynamic time warping) to find the most similar members.
tools.usage:
mdl = pairwiseSimilarityModel
mdl = pairwiseSimilarityModel(Name=Value)
fit(mdl, data, lifeTimeVariable, dataVariables)
estRUL = predictRUL(mdl, data)
tools.notes: Best when the full degradation path, not just its summary, matters.

tools.name: covariateSurvivalModel
tools.description: Creates a proportional-hazards survival RUL model that estimates remaining life from lifetime data plus covariates (e.g. operating conditions, supplier), without requiring condition monitoring histories.
tools.usage:
mdl = covariateSurvivalModel
mdl = covariateSurvivalModel(Name=Value)
fit(mdl, data, lifeTimeVariable, dataVariables, censorVariable)
[estRUL, ciRUL, pdfRUL] = predictRUL(mdl, data)

parameters.name: censorVariable
parameters.description: Variable flagging right-censored (not yet failed) units.

tools.notes: reliabilitySurvivalModel fits a lifetime distribution without covariates; plot(mdl) shows survival curves.

tools.name: reliabilitySurvivalModel
tools.description: Creates a probabilistic failure-time RUL model by fitting a lifetime distribution (Weibull by default) to historical failure times, then predicts RUL of a component given its current age.
tools.usage:
mdl = reliabilitySurvivalModel
mdl = reliabilitySurvivalModel(Name=Value)
fit(mdl, data)
[estRUL, ciRUL, pdfRUL] = predictRUL(mdl, currentLife)
tools.notes: Suited when only failure times are known; accuracy improves with condition-based models when sensor data exist.

tools.name: predictRUL
tools.description: Estimates the remaining useful life of a test component from a trained RUL model (degradation, similarity or survival), returning the estimate, confidence interval and probability distribution of RUL.
tools.usage:
estRUL = predictRUL(mdl, data)
estRUL = predictRUL(mdl, threshold)
[estRUL, ciRUL, pdfRUL] = predictRUL(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: mdl
parameters.description: Any Predictive Maintenance Toolbox RUL model.

parameters.name: data / threshold
parameters.description: Test data (similarity/survival models) or failure threshold (degradation models).

tools.example:
[rul, ci, pdfRUL] = predictRUL(mdl, testMember, Alpha=0.05);
plot(pdfRUL.RUL, pdfRUL.Probability)
tools.notes: Units follow the model's LifeTimeUnit (duration outputs when the lifetime variable is a duration).

tools.name: saveRULModelForCoder
tools.description: Saves a trained RUL model to a MAT-file in a form that can be reloaded with loadRULModelForCoder inside code-generation-compatible functions, enabling deployment of RUL prediction to embedded targets.
tools.usage:
saveRULModelForCoder(mdl, fileName)
mdl = loadRULModelForCoder(fileName)

parameters.name: mdl
parameters.description: Trained degradation or similarity RUL model.

tools.notes: readState/restoreState persist degradation model state between calls on the target.
